Topic1.Title: Call to order, roll call, and agenda amendment
Topic1.Summary: Council convened the regular June 18, 2026 meeting with roll call showing a quorum. Council voted 8-0 to add item 3B, the Colorado Music Festival 50th anniversary declaration, to the agenda.

Topic2.Title: Open comment: Ponderosa Mobile Home Park and housing stability
Topic2.Summary: Ponderosa residents spoke against the Habitat for Humanity stabilization project, citing displacement concerns, a road change affecting homes, lighting and dark sky ordinance issues, and unmet promises about traffic calming. Residents asked for more time and a council liaison. Staff committed to following up with residents.

Topic3.Title: Open comment: minimum wage and tip credit offset
Topic3.Summary: Several speakers, including labor council representatives and tipped workers' advocates, opposed modifying the tip offset, arguing it amounts to a wage cut for tipped workers. Speakers also questioned whether the city's outreach reached restaurant workers. Staff described notification methods including press releases, visits to about 100 restaurants, and the Be Heard Boulder forum.

Topic4.Title: Open comment: Gaza, war industries, and Israel investments
Topic4.Summary: Multiple speakers urged council to recognize genocide in Gaza, divest from Israel, and reduce investments and ties to war industries, while others spoke on anti-Semitism and the definition of anti-Zionism. Council members responded in later comments on anti-Semitism and hate incidents.

Topic5.Title: Open comment: Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan notice and DDA concerns
Topic5.Summary: Speakers raised concerns that the Boulder Valley Comprehensive Plan update notice did not properly reach property owners, and a resident questioned the downtown DDA's revenue diversion from the library, county, and school districts. Staff said the DDA returns to council August 6 and that letters have been sent to partner agencies.

Topic6.Title: Open comment: Fort Chambers interpretive design
Topic6.Summary: A speaker on behalf of Right Relationship Boulder raised concerns that the Fort Chambers interpretive design omits 13,000 years of Native presence and misrepresents Native influence. Staff said they are arranging a meeting with partners and will keep council informed.

Topic7.Title: Council questions to staff on public engagement, racial equity tool, and investments
Topic7.Summary: Council asked how tipped workers were notified and whether the racial equity tool was used in the Right Relationship Boulder matter. Council also asked about the Boulder Valley Comp Plan notice requirements and the status of an investment portfolio review. Staff said an internal review is underway and will be shared with council.

Topic8.Title: Council personal privilege statements on racism and antisemitism
Topic8.Summary: Councilmember Adams reported a racial slur directed at her in a cafe and called for public safety updates on protections for all residents. Councilmembers condemned racism and antisemitism, citing an ADL lawsuit against Boulder Valley School District and an antisemitic incident. Council discussed the need for policy, transparency, and accountability.

Topic9.Title: Juneteenth 2026 declaration
Topic9.Summary: Councilmember Kaplan presented the Juneteenth 2026 declaration to Dr. David Lewis Humphrey. The declaration recognizes June 19 as the end of chattel slavery in the US and encourages community participation in local Juneteenth events.

Topic10.Title: Colorado Music Festival 50th anniversary declaration
Topic10.Summary: Councilmember Marquis presented a declaration naming July 9, 2026 as Colorado Music Festival Day. The festival will present its 50th season at Chautauqua Auditorium and draws more than 20,000 attendees annually.

Topic11.Title: Consent agenda
Topic11.Summary: Council approved consent agenda items 4A through 4D unanimously on a motion and second with roll call vote.

Topic12.Title: Call-up check-ins
Topic12.Summary: Council reviewed two call-up items: concept plan review for redevelopment of the Unity Church property at 2855 Folsom with 21 detached dwellings, and a landmark alteration certificate to demolish an accessory building at 1039 Mapleton Avenue. No council member called either item up.

Topic13.Title: Spring Valley Estates annexation and resolution 1381
Topic13.Summary: Council held a public hearing on the annexation of about 43 acres in Spring Valley Estates with RE initial zoning, approved by election. Staff explained the phased process, required water and road infrastructure, and a local improvement district. Council adopted resolution 1381 unanimously and approved an agreement with the Spring Valley Mutual Water Association. Council discussed DOLA grant timing, the 90-day election blackout, and cost allocation concerns raised by residents.

Topic14.Title: Ordinance 8751 on special festival events
Topic14.Summary: Council held a public hearing and adopted ordinance 8751 unanimously. It creates a permit process and standards for special festival events such as Sundance, updates mobile food vehicle rules, and adds sign code provisions for temporary event signage. Staff said the ordinance would take effect in 30 days and be monitored.

Topic15.Title: Ordinance 8752 on festival liquor licenses
Topic15.Summary: Council held a public hearing and adopted ordinance 8752 unanimously. It allows festival liquor licenses and permits authorized by state law and sets a $150 local application fee for administrative review. Council discussed fee-setting and cost recovery.

Topic16.Title: Council employee evaluation timeline
Topic16.Summary: Councilmember Spear shared the timeline for the council employee evaluation process. The survey launches July 7 and closes July 28, with summaries due in August and a consent agenda item on September 3.
